previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of atrial fibrillation, diastolic heart failure, moderate aortic stenosis with regurgitation, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for worsening muscle twitching and lethargy. He had a recent episode of dark emesis and was found to have uremia with elevated creatinine and BUN, hyponatremia, and a supratherapeutic INR. The twitching was attributed to uremia secondary to poor forward flow from heart failure. He was treated with IV diuresis, which improved his kidney function, resolved his asterixis, and stabilized his electrolytes. His INR was corrected with vitamin K, followed by bridging with heparin and restarting warfarin at a lower dose. Pulmonary edema was managed with increased furosemide, and he was transitioned to 40 mg daily at discharge. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged to extended care with a cardiology follow-up, daily weight monitoring, and instructions on fluid and sodium restriction.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old ___ speaking male with a history of atrial 
fibrillation on warfarin, diastolic CHF, severe AS w/ 
mild-moderate aortic regurgitation, moderate pulmonary artery 
systolic hypertension, chronic bronchitis, hypertension, and 
past TIAs presenting p/w RLE erythema/swelling and worsening SOB 
x 4d.

# dyspnea: most likely CHF exacerbation given symptomatic 
improvement w/ diuresis. Pt was treated initially with iv 
furosemide but then switched to his prior home dose of 
furosemide 40mg po daily (which was recently lowered to 30mg). 
His oxygen requirement resolved with diuresis. He was seen by 
___, nurse practitioner for Dr ___, on ___ 
whose final assessment was that his heart failure flare had 
completely resolved and that he had no evidence of volume 
overload. This was also discussed with Dr ___ was in 
agreement with ___ findings. He will follow up with Dr 
___ on ___ at 1:40 ___. It was explained to 
the patient and is son that with his severe aortic stenosis he 
will have some baseline shortness of breadth. His son raised the 
question of surgical intervention and it was discussed with him 
that this is a   complex decision in a ___ year old man and he 
will discuss this further with Dr ___ on follow up.

# R lower extremity cellulitis: His leg was warm, tender, 
erythematous and edematous on exam consistent with cellulitis.  
Lower extremity dopplers were negative for DVTs. Blood cultures 
were performed which were negative. There was no sepsis in the 
blood stream. He was initially treated with vancomycin, switched 
to oral treatment with doxycycline and keflex, but due to 
reluctance to take oral antibiotics, switched back to 
vancomycin. This was discussed with his son who explained that 
his reluctance to take orals was due to abdominal discomfort if 
oral antibiotics were taken prior to food. He was switched back 
to oral keflex and doxycyline given after food. In total he 
received a 10 day course of antibiotics for treatment of his 
cellulitis which is a full treatment course. He will receive his 
last dose of keflex at the rehabilitation facility tonight. 
He has had 2 episodes of cellulitis in four months. Once an 
individual has had an episode of cellulitis, they are 
predisposed to recurrent episodes, often in the same limb,due to 
soft tissue changes predisoposing to recurrent infection. 
Further episodes can be avoided by empiric treatment if his feet 
with antifungals as skin breakage due to fungal infection is 
often a predisposing factor. He is discharged with miconazole 2% 
cream twice a day applied to both feet for two weeks. 
Additionally he is encouraged to elevate his feet above the 
level of his heart at bedtime to improve circulation. 
.
# diastolic CHF: medically optimize. Pt's digoxin level was 0.4 
on admission. His digoxin dose was previously 0.125 mcg po every 
other day due to previously elevated levels. Pt was discharged 
on digoxin 0.125mcg daily. His levels will need to be followed 
daily. His home metoprolol and diltiazem were continued. His 
furosemide dose was 40mg daily on discharge and weight was 
53.8kg.

# atrial fibrillation: subtherapeutic on admission w/ INR 1.4. 
Home dose 3.5mg daily. Given CHADS2 score of 4 and stagnant INR 
plus past history of TIAs, Pt was bridged with enoxaparin 70mg 
sc bid while awaiting INR to become therapeutic range.  The 
enoxaparin and warfarin were held when he developed spontaneous 
bleeding. Once the bleeding has stopped, the warfarin was 
retarted at a dose of 5mg daily and downtitrated to 4mg daily at 
discharge to maintain his INR in the range of ___. His INR was 
2.5 on ___.  He was discharged with digoxin 0.125mcg daily 
with a digoxin level of 1 of ___. 

#Hypercoagulability: Pt was bridged with enoxaparin 70mg sc bid 
while awaiting INR to become therapeutic range. In this setting 
he became over anticoagulated and experienced spontaneous 
bleeding at multiple sites. He had a picc line placed in his 
left antecubital fossa for IV vancomycin delivery, but 
experienced spontaneous bleeding at this site, which resolved 
with extended pressure. He also experienced spontaneous bleeding 
with hematomas on his right posterior shin, his right abdomen 
and his right shoulder,all of which are improving. Due to 
bleeding in his right shoulder joint he had a X-ray of the 
shoulder which revealed a hematoma, and he was evaluated by 
orthopedics The orthopedics consult team discussed this with his 
outpatient Orthopedic physician, ___ there was 
agreement that he should not have aspiration performed, but 
conservative management with pain control and elevation of the 
right arm, as well as daily exercises to maintain range of 
motion at the right shoulder.  The orthopedic consult team 
instructed that a MRI was not indicated (this was raised as a 
question in the radiology report) and indicated that there was 
no sepsis in the right shoulder joint. Pain was treated with 
tylenol with codeine and lidocaine patch. He will follow up with 
Dr ___ on ___ at 2:00pm.
.
# Apthous ulcers: He developed apthous ulcers on his tongue and 
buccal mucosa in the setting of acute systemic illness with oral 
pain. Pain was controlled with viscous lidocaine. He will 
continue viscous lidocaine on discharge. 
.

INDICATION:  ___ male with shortness of breath and history of
congestive heart failure.  Evaluate.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal and PA and lateral chest radiographs.

FINDINGS:  There are diffusely increased bilateral interstitial markings, with
associated bibasilar focal consolidations, right worse than left,  that
obscure the margins of both hemidiaphragms and the right heart border. There
is no evidence of pneumothorax.  Heart size cannot be accurately assessed due
to obscuration of sillouhette by basilar consolidations. Severe
atherosclerotic calcification of the aorta is present.

IMPRESSION:  
1.  Findings compatible with interstitial pulmonary edema in the setting of
known cardiomegaly. 
2.  Bibasilar opacities, right greater than left, may be the result of a
combination of bilateral lower lobe atelectasis and pleural effusions,
underlying consolidation, particularly in the right lower lobe is of concern. 
3.  Right middle lobe atelectasis is also present.

INDICATION:  Right lower extremity edema.

COMPARISONS:  Right lower extremity ultrasound ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale, Doppler, and spectral ultrasound images were acquired
through the right lower extremity.

FINDINGS:  The bilateral common femoral veins demonstrate normal flow and
respiratory variation.  The right common femoral vein, superficial femoral
vein, and popliteal vein demonstrate normal flow, compressibility, and
response to augmentation.  The right peroneal and posterior tibial veins
demonstrate normal flow.  There is moderate subcutaneous edema in the right
calf.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of right lower extremity deep vein thrombosis.
2.  Moderate right calf subcutaneous edema.

STUDY:  Right ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ male on Lovenox with right shoulder swelling
and petechiae.  Evaluate for hemarthrosis.

FINDINGS:  Comparison is made to radiographs of the chest from ___
as well as of the shoulder from ___.

There are again seen severe end-stage osteoarthritic changes involving the
right glenohumeral joint.  There is flattening of the medial aspect of the
humerus as well as of the glenoid.  There is a large soft tissue density
lateral to the humeral head.  This may represent a large joint effusion or
hematoma.  There is also a pressure erosion involving the undersurface of the
acromion and clavicle which may be due to rotator cuff rupture.  The humeral
head does not articulate with the acromion, possibly due to bursitis and joint
effusion or hematoma.  No acute fractures are seen.  The visualized right lung
apex is clear.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Increased soft tissue density along the superolateral aspect of the right
shoulder soft tissues.  This may represent a hematoma.  Alternatively, this
may represent bursitis related to joint fluid in the subacromial/subdeltoid
bursa.  If there is high concern, MRI could be performed.

2.  Severe end-stage osteoarthritic changes involving the right glenohumeral
joint with flattening of the medial aspect of the humerus and of the glenoid.

3.  Undersurface erosion involving the acromion and clavicle likely
representing chronic rotator cuff injury, stable.
